# Measured results

Generated by `npm run report` (scripts/report.ts), on Node v22.23.4. Reference libraries: Python 3.12.3, libigl 2.6.3, potpourri3d 1.4.0, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, mpmath 1.4.1, meshio 5.3.5.

Every number in the README's results section is copied from the summary below. Times are from one run on one machine and will differ on yours; everything else is deterministic.

## Summary

<!-- results:start (generated by npm run report; do not edit) -->

- **Gauss–Bonnet.** The angle defects sum to 2πχ within 1.4e-13 on 840 random meshes (discs, spheres and tori, before and after edge flips). This checks the connectivity and each triangle's angle sum; the individual angles are checked against libigl and mpmath below.
- **Curvature.** On a regular grid the pointwise error falls at order 1.70 to 1.92 (2.4e+0, 7.3e-1, 1.9e-1, 5.2e-2 at 8, 16, 32, 64 cells per side). With 15% vertex jitter it stops falling (2.2e+0, 9.9e-1, 5.2e-1, 5.5e-1); angle defects are known to converge pointwise only on regular meshes. A cone's apex defect is right to 2.2e-16.
- **Intrinsic Delaunay.** Of 3,000 random bumps, 0 stop short of Delaunay; 20 of the 3,000 need parallel edges or loops to get there. Flipping changes no vertex's curvature by more than 2.7e-15.
- **Spectrum.** The first ten eigenvalues of the unit square converge at order 1.98 to 2.04; at 24 cells per side the worst is off by 1.4%.
- **Geodesic distance.** From a cone's apex or a sphere's pole, where the problem is symmetric, the largest error against the exact distance falls at order 2.00 to 2.00 and 1.98 to 2.00. From a general vertex it falls far more slowly: order 0.67 to 0.98 on the cone (1.8e-1, 9.3e-2, 4.8e-2, 3.0e-2) and 0.47 to 0.83 on the sphere (2.4e-1, 1.3e-1, 8.5e-2, 6.1e-2). That is how the method behaves with its standard time step, not an implementation defect: the same distances agree with potpourri3d's to the fifth digit.
- **Reference libraries.** Face areas are bit-identical to libigl's. The stiffness matrix differs from libigl's by 4.0e-16 (relative), eigenvalues from LAPACK's by 1.8e-14, heat-method distances from an independent SciPy implementation by 1.8e-14 and from potpourri3d by 2.0e-5. That last gap is one line of geometry-central, a 1e-6 shift of the Laplacian: with the same shift the SciPy implementation matches potpourri3d to 2.9e-15.
- **Thin triangles.** On 185 needle-shaped triangles, area and angles are within 1.93 and 2.12 units of roundoff of 80-digit arithmetic. The textbook Heron formula is wrong beyond 1e-8 on 85 of them.

<!-- results:end -->

## Curvature from angle defects

Gaussian bump, height 0.6 and width 0.45, over the square [−1, 1]². Largest |K − K exact| over interior vertices, where K is the angle defect divided by the mixed Voronoi area.

| Cells per side | Regular grid | Order | 15% jitter |
| -------------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------- |
| 8              | 2.4e+0       |       | 2.2e+0     |
| 16             | 7.3e-1       | 1.70  | 9.9e-1     |
| 32             | 1.9e-1       | 1.92  | 5.2e-1     |
| 64             | 5.2e-2       | 1.90  | 5.5e-1     |

The jittered column is not a defect of this implementation. Angle-defect curvature converges pointwise only on meshes with special regularity (Borrelli, Cazals and Morvan 2003). The total over the mesh is exact because it is topological: the Gauss–Bonnet sum is within 1.4e-13 of 2πχ on all 840 random meshes tried. That sum checks the connectivity and each triangle's angle sum, not the individual angles; it would also hold if every angle were replaced by π/3.

## Intrinsic Delaunay triangulation

3,000 Gaussian bumps with random resolution (1 to 14 cells per side), jitter, height and width: 110,699 flips in all. 0 end with a non-Delaunay edge. 20 end as a triangulation that is not a simplicial complex (two edges between the same vertices, or a loop). Largest change in any vertex's angle defect: 2.7e-15.

## Spectrum of the unit square

Relative error of the first ten non-zero Neumann eigenvalues, which are π²(m² + n²).

| Cells per side | Smallest error | Largest error |
| -------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| 6              | 4.8e-3         | 2.1e-1        |
| 12             | 1.1e-3         | 5.5e-2        |
| 24             | 2.7e-4         | 1.4e-2        |

Order of convergence between 12 and 24 cells, per eigenvalue: 2.00, 2.03, 2.04, 2.00, 1.99, 2.00, 2.03, 2.04, 1.98, 1.99.

Dense symmetric eigensolver on random matrices:

| Size | Largest residual of A v − λ v | Time   |
| ---- | ----------------------------- | ------ |
| 289  | 3.0e-14                       | 0.17 s |
| 625  | 1.9e-14                       | 1.14 s |
| 1089 | 8.8e-14                       | 6.13 s |

### Why a direct solver

One backward-Euler heat step from a corner of a 65 × 65 grid (4,225 vertices). The smallest true value is 7.4e-37. Conjugate gradients at a relative residual of 1e-15 stop after 51 iterations with 2,530 values that are zero or negative; the sparse Cholesky solve has 0. The method needs the direction of the gradient of those tiny values.

| Vertices | Numbers in the factor | Factor | Solve  |
| -------- | --------------------- | ------ | ------ |
| 1,089    | 25,553                | 1 ms   | 0.1 ms |
| 4,225    | 189,345               | 12 ms  | 0.8 ms |
| 16,641   | 1,455,937             | 135 ms | 6.9 ms |

## Agreement with reference libraries

From `oracle/measure_agreement.py`, on 7 meshes, 14 distance cases and 185 thin triangles. Differences are relative to the largest value compared, except the angle defect, which is absolute.

| Quantity                        | Reference                                   | Largest difference     |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Face areas                      | libigl                                      | identical              |
| Angle defect                    | libigl                                      | 2.6e-15                |
| Cotan stiffness matrix          | libigl                                      | 4.0e-16                |
| Laplacian after Delaunay flips  | libigl                                      | 6.8e-16                |
| Eigenvalues                     | LAPACK (SciPy)                              | 1.8e-14                |
| Heat-method distance            | SciPy re-implementation                     | 1.8e-14                |
| Heat-method distance            | potpourri3d                                 | 2.0e-5                 |
| potpourri3d                     | SciPy re-implementation with its 1e-6 shift | 2.9e-15                |
| Triangle area, thin triangles   | mpmath, 80 digits                           | 1.93 units of roundoff |
| Triangle angles, thin triangles | mpmath, 80 digits                           | 2.12 units of roundoff |
